claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution with a uniform elemental distribution.
The metastable solid solution gradually decomposes by a diffusional process during aging.
Mg segregates during aging and nucleates fine, metastable Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds nucleate predominantly at grain boundaries.
Local compositional fluctuations drive Mg segregation during aging.
Mg-rich intermetallic phases act as preferential sites for oxide nucleation.
A fine, discontinuous dispersion of Mg-rich intermetallics can stabilize a protective oxide layer.
Coarse or continuous intermetallic networks can provide fast diffusion paths for oxygen and corrosive species.
Fast transport through coarse or continuous intermetallic networks degrades passivation.
Aging at approximately 400–550°C will produce Mg-rich intermetallic phases relative to the initial metastable state.
Aging-induced intermetallic formation will modify oxide-scale characteristics and oxidation kinetics.
Corrosion resistance after aging will vary with the distribution and connectivity of the intermetallic phases.
The relevant service-temperature regime is approximately 400–550°C in oxidizing or corrosive atmospheres.
Outside the proposed service-temperature range, rapid transformation kinetics may alter the observed performance trends.
